svg.title: Four Buckets Allocate the $55,000 Reference Budget
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-lean-reference-expanded-startup-allocation; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Four Buckets Allocate the $55,000 Reference Budget; subtitle: Startup capital: $20,000–$95,000 USD; compare $20,000 lean, $55,000 reference, and $95,000 expanded.; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Numeric values are USD in the central $55,000 reference startup plan, within the canonical $20,000–$95,000 range. Each bucket uses the same percentage at the $20,000 lean and $95,000 expanded endpoints, allowing proportional stacked comparison. Capital allocations are funding uses, not annual expense or revenue. The reference allocation is not an additional earnings scenario or a guarantee of sufficient runway.; caption: All four buckets reconcile at each funding level: $20,000 lean, $55,000 reference, and $95,000 expanded. Monthly opex remains $4,000–$18,000 and time to first deal remains 2–7 months; match commitments to funded liquidity rather than assuming the cash buffer covers the entire launch. Inventory purchases are not profit.; stages: label: Equipment acquisition reserve; value: $27,500 reference allocation | 50% of capital; numeric value: 27500.0; detail: Lean stack: $10,000; reference stack: $27,500; expanded stack: $47,500. Fund serial-defined inventory within per-model exposure limits and documented buyer demand. Keep unsold equipment on the inventory ledger and review aging weekly.; label: Refurbishment and testing capacity; value: $11,000 reference allocation | 20% of capital; numeric value: 11000.0; detail: Lean stack: $4,000; reference stack: $11,000; expanded stack: $19,000. Fund inspection, parts, bench work, calibrated test equipment access, decontamination, and service documentation. Separate durable tooling from unit-level inventory costs.; label: Operating cash buffer; value: $13,750 reference allocation | 25% of capital; numeric value: 13750.0; detail: Lean stack: $5,000; reference stack: $13,750; expanded stack: $23,750. At the modeled $11,958 monthly Base-Case overhead, the reference buffer covers about 1.15 months before direct inventory spending, shorter than the 2–7 month first-deal window. Phase commitments, reduce launch burn, or secure additional liquidity before taking on unfunded obligations.; label: Setup and transaction reserve; value: $2,750 reference allocation | 5% of capital; numeric value: 2750.0; detail: Lean stack: $1,000; reference stack: $2,750; expanded stack: $4,750. Fund insurance deposits, inventory-system setup, initial packing materials, and specialist classification review. Track refundable deposits separately from expenses and avoid duplicating operating-buffer charges.

text.title: Four Buckets Allocate the $55,000 Reference Budget

rect.title: label: Equipment acquisition reserve; numeric value: 27500.0; value: $27,500 reference allocation | 50% of capital; detail: Lean stack: $10,000; reference stack: $27,500; expanded stack: $47,500. Fund serial-defined inventory within per-model exposure limits and documented buyer demand. Keep unsold equipment on the inventory ledger and review aging weekly.

text.title: Equipment acquisition reserve: $27,500 reference allocation | 50% of capital
text.tspan: Equipment acquisition reserve: $27,500 reference allocation | 50% of capital

rect.title: label: Refurbishment and testing capacity; numeric value: 11000.0; value: $11,000 reference allocation | 20% of capital; detail: Lean stack: $4,000; reference stack: $11,000; expanded stack: $19,000. Fund inspection, parts, bench work, calibrated test equipment access, decontamination, and service documentation. Separate durable tooling from unit-level inventory costs.

text.title: Refurbishment and testing capacity: $11,000 reference allocation | 20% of capital
text.tspan: Refurbishment and testing capacity: $11,000 reference allocation | 20% of capital

rect.title: label: Operating cash buffer; numeric value: 13750.0; value: $13,750 reference allocation | 25% of capital; detail: Lean stack: $5,000; reference stack: $13,750; expanded stack: $23,750. At the modeled $11,958 monthly Base-Case overhead, the reference buffer covers about 1.15 months before direct inventory spending, shorter than the 2–7 month first-deal window. Phase commitments, reduce launch burn, or secure additional liquidity before taking on unfunded obligations.
